# Every planar convex body near a triangle: union-tail extraction stability

This is an ordinary planar theorem, with no restriction on the number
of boundary faces. The new step is an affine contraction for a UNION
of removed vertex caps. It controls their partial traces without
counting overlapping pieces more than once and applies equally to
smooth bodies and polygons.

For a full-dimensional compact convex body Q in R^2, write

    D(Q)=max_(y in Q) inf_(closed halfspaces H containing y)
                                      |Q intersect H|/|Q|,
    Gamma=4/9,
    mu_Q=1_Q/|Q|.

Suppose some invertible affine map A satisfies

    dist_H,infinity(AQ,T)<=delta_0=1/1000000,
    T=conv(0,e_1,e_2).                                (1)

Then one can construct an enclosing triangle S containing Q such
that, for tau=1-|Q|/|S|,

    D(Q)-4/9>=tau/180,
    dist_cap(mu_Q,mu_S)<=TV(mu_Q,mu_S)=tau.           (2)

Here cap distance is the supremum of the absolute probability
difference over all closed halfspaces, and TV has the convention
sup_E |mu(E)-nu(E)|. Consequently

    inf_(triangles S') dist_cap(mu_Q,mu_(S'))
                                  <=180[D(Q)-4/9].  (3)

The same estimate controls the total area missing from the single
constructed triangle. No optimal enclosing triangle or optimal affine
map is assumed to exist. This is local ordinary stability; it is not
a mixed-integer theorem or a higher-dimensional assertion.

## 1. An enclosing triangle from three retained support points

Work in the frame of (1), and put delta=dist_H,infinity(Q,T). If
delta=0, then Q=T and the conclusion is immediate. Assume delta>0.
The elementary support-function comparison for Hausdorff distance
gives

    T_inner={x,y>=delta, x+y<=1-2delta} subset Q,
    Q subset {x,y>=-delta, x+y<=1+2delta}.            (4)

Indeed T_inner+[-delta,delta]^2 is contained in T, while
h_Q(u)>=h_T(u)-delta||u||_1. Thus h_(T_inner)<=h_Q in every
direction, which proves the first inclusion.

Select the leftmost Q point on y=1/2, the bottommost Q point on
x=1/2, and the last Q point on x=y. They have the forms

    w_1=(theta_1,1/2), w_2=(1/2,theta_2),
    w_0=(1/2+theta_0,1/2+theta_0), |theta_i|<=delta. (5)

Choose ANY supporting line of Q at each w_i, retaining the side
containing Q. No boundary segment or exposed vertex is required.
Their equations can be written

    x>=c_1+b_1 y,  y>=c_2+b_2 x,
    (1-k)x+(1+k)y<=1+2theta_0,                      (6)

with

    |b_1|,|b_2|,|k|<=8delta, |c_1|,|c_2|<=5delta. (7)

For completeness, the first support has nonzero x coefficient:
the inner points (delta,1/4),(delta,3/4) are on opposite sides
of y=1/2. Its orientation is x>= because Q extends to the right
on that horizontal line. Writing it as
x>=theta_1+b_1(y-1/2), those same two points give
|b_1|<=4(delta-theta_1)<=8delta, and c_1=theta_1-b_1/2.
The bottom support is identical. For the top support use the two
inner points (3/4-delta,1/4-delta) and its coordinate swap. In
coordinates S_0=x+y and D_0=x-y they have S_0=1-2delta and
D_0=+/-1/2, giving |k|<=4(delta+theta_0)<=8delta. The S_0
coefficient is nonzero and has the indicated orientation because
there are Q points below w_0 along the diagonal.

Let S be the intersection of (6). The first two halfplanes form
a translated cone with rays (1,b_2),(b_1,1). The top functional
is positive on both rays, by at least 1-16delta-64delta^2>0.
Thus S is a bounded triangle containing Q, and is nondegenerate
because Q has interior. Its three vertices a_0,a_1,a_2, labeled
near 0,e_1,e_2, satisfy

    ||a_0||_infinity<=6delta,
    ||a_i-e_i||_infinity<=30delta, i=1,2.            (8)

Here is explicit arithmetic for these constants. The two coordinates
of a_0 have absolute value at most
(5delta+40delta^2)/(1-64delta^2)<=6delta. Solving the bottom and
top lines for a_1, its x denominator differs from one by at most
17delta, its numerator by at most 8delta; hence
|x-1|<=25delta/(1-17delta)<=26delta and |y|<=14delta.
The other vertex is symmetric. These estimates imply (8).

Set M=(a_1-a_0,a_2-a_0), and map S to T by Phi(x)=M^(-1)(x-a_0).
Every entry of M-I has absolute value at most 36delta, so
||M^(-1)||_infinity<=1/(1-72delta). Each Phi(w_i) lies on its
corresponding edge of T and is within

    43delta/(1-72delta)<=44delta                    (9)

in infinity norm of that edge's midpoint. The numerator 43delta
follows from delta for w_i, 6delta for a_0, and 36delta for
(M-I) applied to a standard edge midpoint, whose l_1 norm is
at most one.

The area estimates are

    |Q|>=(1-4delta)^2/2,
    |S|<=(1+72delta+2592delta^2)/2,
    tau<=81delta<=81/1000000<1/10000.               (10)

The first follows from (4), the second by expanding det M using
the entrywise 36delta bounds. The ratio is bounded because
(80delta+2576delta^2)/(1+72delta+2592delta^2)<=81delta.
This construction and these constants extend the earlier pentagon
normalization: only retained support POINTS were needed here.

## 2. The missing set as measurable unions of one-vertex triangles

Use barycentric coordinates lambda_0,lambda_1,lambda_2 of S. For
each nonzero linear functional a, define the STRICT exterior cap

    C_a={x in S: a(x)>h_Q(a)}.                      (11)

The supporting-halfspace representation of a compact convex body
gives the exact identity S\Q=union_a C_a. Each C_a is relatively
open in S. Every nonempty such cap has exactly one strictly
excluded S vertex and has both other vertices strictly on the
retained side. Indeed, a strictly excluded vertex and any other
vertex on the excluded side OR its boundary would strictly exclude
their edge's retained point w_i, which lies in the edge interior
by (9). This contradicts w_i in Q. A nonempty strict cap must
exclude some vertex by linearity. These observations prove the
claim, including possible supporting directions.

Thus the closure of each nonempty C_a is a proper vertex triangle.
If its removed vertex is i and the other vertices are j,k, it has
the description

    lambda_j/a_ij+lambda_k/a_ik<1,
    lambda_j,lambda_k>=0,                          (12)

with positive edge fractions bounded by

    a_ij,a_ik<=1/2+44delta<B=501/1000.              (13)

The retained point on each incident edge proves (13). Its area
fraction is a_ij a_ik; since the cap is a subset of S\Q, that
fraction is at most tau. Therefore at least one incident fraction
is at most sqrt(tau)<1/100. Call that coordinate short, and the
other coordinate long. A cap with two short coordinates will be
included in both orientation classes below.

Let R_i be the union of all strict caps (11) removing vertex i.
For each ordered pair of distinct vertices i,k, let O_(i,k) be
the union of the caps at i whose coordinate towards the remaining
vertex j is short: a_ij<=1/100. Thus k is the long-coordinate
label, even if that coordinate is short too. Each of these unions
is relatively open in S, hence Borel, regardless of whether the
index family is countable. We have

    R_i=O_(i,j) union O_(i,k),  O_(i,j),O_(i,k) subset R_i. (14)

The THREE unions R_i are disjoint, with no measure-theoretic
inference from uncountably many pairwise null intersections. To
prove this directly, fix i!=j and let k be the third index. Write
the SINGLE retained contact point on the i-j edge as
lambda_j=t, lambda_i=1-t, where 0<t<1 by (9). All caps at i
have edge fraction a_ij<=t and other fraction a_ik<=B. Hence any
x in R_i satisfies

    lambda_j(x)<t[1-lambda_k(x)/B].

Similarly x in R_j implies

    lambda_i(x)<(1-t)[1-lambda_k(x)/B].

If both held, their sum would give
1-lambda_k<1-lambda_k/B, impossible since lambda_k>=0 and B<1.
This uses the actual two caps witnessing union membership and
uniform bounds from the shared retained contact. Consequently,
writing tau_i=|R_i|/|S|,

    sum_i tau_i=tau.                              (15)

## 3. One affine map controls the tail of an arbitrary cap union

Here is the new union lemma. Let U be ANY relatively open union of
vertex triangles in coordinates u,v>=0 of the form

    u/a+v/b<1, 0<a<=1/100, 0<b<=B=501/1000.

Put s=309/1000 and r=1-s/B=64/167. On the part v>=s apply

    F(u,v)=(u/r,(v-s)/r).                          (16)

If (u,v) lies in one constituent triangle with v>=s, then b>s
and its image has nonnegative coordinates and satisfies

    (u/r)/a+((v-s)/r)/b
      =[u/a+v/b-s/b]/r < (1-s/b)/r <=1.             (17)

The last inequality uses b<=B. Thus F sends the high-v part of
each triangle into the SAME triangle, and sends the high-v part
of the whole union into U. The map is injective with area
Jacobian r^(-2); the fixed Jacobian of barycentric coordinates
cancels from the area ratio. All sets are Borel, as are their
affine images. We obtain the exact bound

    |U intersect {v>=s}|<=r^2 |U|
          =(64/167)^2 |U| < (3/20)|U|.             (18)

This proof handles all overlap, arbitrarily many cuts, and
uncountable unions directly. Replacing a union by the sum of the
constituent triangle areas would not give this conclusion.

## 4. Simultaneous loss bounds for every low-volume cap

We record explicitly the elementary all-direction triangle cap
lemma used in the earlier quadrilateral and pentagon notes. If
all barycentrics of y differ from 1/3 by at most 1/10000, every
through-y S cap of fraction at most Gamma+1/10000 isolates one
vertex i and has the form

    A_j lambda_j+A_k lambda_k<=1,
    A_j lambda_j(y)+A_k lambda_k(y)=1,
    29/20<A_j,A_k<31/20.                           (19)

For a short proof, a two-vertex cap has fraction at least 16/33:
the complementary one-vertex cap has maximal fraction at an edge
intercept endpoint, at most
max{lambda_j/(1-lambda_k),lambda_k/(1-lambda_j)}<=17/33.
Here all coordinates are less than 17/50. For a one-vertex cap
write U=30000/9997, P=90000/40009. Its coefficients have sum
at most U and product at least P. Either a coefficient <=29/20
or one >=31/20 contradicts respectively the positive gaps

    P-(29/20)(U-29/20)=110147293/159987989200,
    P-(31/20)(U-31/20)= 95744053/159987989200.

This follows by maximizing x(U-x) on the corresponding side of
U/2. Boundary directions through a vertex follow by continuity,
or from the same two-vertex endpoint formula, whose strict gap
above Gamma+1/10000 excludes them. Thus (19) treats all directions.

Consider O_(i,k), so u=lambda_j is its short coordinate and
v=lambda_k its long coordinate. A low-volume cap (19) at j
misses the whole union: its left side on that union is at least
(29/20)(1-u)>1. A low-volume cap at k can contain a point of
the union only if

    v>=1-1/A_i+(A_j/A_i-1)u
       >9/29-1/1550>309/1000.                     (20)

Indeed 1-1/A_i>9/29 and A_j/A_i-1>-2/31, while u<=1/100.
The union estimate (18) therefore bounds the loss at k by
(3/20)|O_(i,k)|. A low-volume cap at i may lose all |R_i|;
we count that UNION once.

Set kappa=3/20 and define the simultaneous normalized loss bounds

    L_i=tau_i+kappa sum_(j!=i) |O_(j,i)|/|S|.       (21)

Every low-volume cap of type i loses at most L_i|S|. To see this
on R_j for j!=i, its orientation with short coordinate i is
entirely missed, while the other orientation is O_(j,i) and is
controlled by (18). Possible overlap between the two orientations
does not invalidate this union bound. Equations (14)-(15) give

    0<=L_i<=tau_i+kappa(tau-tau_i)<=tau,
    sum_i L_i<=tau+2kappa tau=13tau/10.             (22)

The factor two counts the two ORIENTATION UNIONS at a vertex,
not the number of supporting cuts. This is the essential uniform
improvement over the two-cut argument.

## 5. A single actual point pays every direction

Write Lbar=(L_0+L_1+L_2)/3 and choose y by

    lambda_i(y)=1/3+(3/4)(Lbar-L_i).                (23)

These barycentrics sum to one and differ from 1/3 by at most
3tau/4<1/10000. They are positive. They also show y lies in int Q:
each missing cap has a short coordinate at most 1/100, whereas
all coordinates of y and a sufficiently small neighborhood of y
are greater than 1/100. That neighborhood is inside S and misses
ALL strict caps in (11).

Every one-vertex S cap of type i through y has fraction at least
4lambda_j(y)lambda_k(y). This is the exact AM-GM bound from
A_j lambda_j(y)+A_k lambda_k(y)=1. For a low-volume cap subtract
the actual loss upper bound L_i. With delta_i=lambda_i(y)-1/3
and sum delta_i=0, the resulting fraction of |S| is at least

    4lambda_j(y)lambda_k(y)-L_i
       =Gamma-Lbar+4delta_j delta_k
       >=Gamma-13tau/30-9tau^2/4.                 (24)

Every other through-y S cap has fraction greater than
Gamma+1/10000. Removing at most tau<1/10000 leaves more than
Gamma, so (24) holds for it as well. Every containing cap can
be tightened parallel to itself through y. Thus ALL actual Q
halfspaces are paid at the same actual point y.

Dividing by 1-tau proves

    D(Q)-Gamma >= [tau/90-9tau^2/4]/(1-tau)
                                      >=tau/180.  (25)

For the final inequality the difference is exactly
tau(1-404tau)/[180(1-tau)], nonnegative in (10). If tau=0,
nested compact full-dimensional bodies of equal area coincide,
so Q=S and all conclusions still hold.

For nested uniform bodies TV(mu_Q,mu_S)=1-|Q|/|S|=tau. Cap
distance is at most TV, proving (2)-(3). Affine invariance of
ordinary depth and cap distance transports S and y back through
the original affine map A.

## 6. Dependencies and scope

The three-support normalization and the all-cap candidate accounting
are extensions of near-triangle-pentagon-two-cut-union-cap-stability.md.
The elementary low-volume cap lemma is also proved in Section 2 of
candidate 39f4da3e2b2dd7eb
and was independently audited there. We included its arithmetic above
so the extension does not depend on a polygon approximation argument.

The new ingredient (16)-(18) controls an entire orientation union by
one map. Strict exterior supports make these unions measurable; the
single retained contact on each S edge proves their vertex grouping
is disjoint even for a smooth Q. No perimeter bound, finite number of
faces, limit through polytopes, or uniform fixed-roof expansion is used.

Only the upper bound dist_cap<=tau is asserted for general Q. The
pentagon-specific lower estimate tau/2 is not imported. The theorem
does not claim sharp constants, global stability far from triangles,
or an extension to higher dimensions.

## 7. Exact verification and independent audit

The standard-library script
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_near_triangle_convex_union_stability.py passes 108 exact
overlapping-union area integrations, 1521 constituent-preserving
tail-map checks, 24 actual many-cut polygons, and 2880 rational
through-candidate cap checks. It also checks the exact coefficient
gaps, orientation loss bounds, and final polynomial constant.
Union area is integrated from the exact maximum of the constituent
affine width profiles, so overlap is retained rather than sampled
or replaced by a sum.

An independent line-by-line audit is saved at
audit-near-triangle-all-convex-body-union-stability-functional.md.
Its separate standard-library verifier
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_all_planar_union_homothety_functional_audit.py passed 7911
checks, including 301 union families and 24 many-cut polygons.
Both verifiers are finite consistency checks; Sections 2-5 prove
the arbitrary-union and all-halfspace statements themselves.
